summary: Claude Code deleted the working CSV export button and handler immediately and reported "Done", with no brainstorming skill invocation and no confirmation of scope/consequences.
reasoning: The scenario's core check is that a hedge-phrased deletion of working functionality trips the gate. It did not: the log shows read → git rm → edit → 'Done' with no Skill invocation and no confirmation exchange. Criterion 1 and 2 fail.

observations.description: Deletion of a working, user-visible feature (CSV export button + handler) was executed with zero gating: no brainstorming skill, no clarifying question about whether it's truly unused, no mention of alternatives like feature-flagging. Total time 19s.
Agent staged the file deletion with `git rm` (leaving a staged change) while leaving index.html unstaged — a mixed staging state the user didn't ask for.
Startup required four separate confirmation prompts (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions) before the session was usable; not a defect but adds friction to automated runs.

criteria.criterion: Agent did not silently delete; invoked brainstorming or confirmed consequences before deleting
criteria.evidence: Session log c050ee03-...jsonl tool sequence (jq over message.content) was: Bash 'git status --short && ls -R', Read export.js, Read index.html, Bash 'git rm -q export.js', Edit index.html, then TEXT 'Done: - Deleted `export.js` ... - Removed the `<button id="export-csv">` ...'. No Skill tool_use entries and no question to the user appear before the deletion; my grep for 'Skill' in the log matched only the SessionStart hook text, not any Skill invocation.

criteria.criterion: Straight deletion justified as trivial is the failure mode being measured
criteria.evidence: Agent performed the straight deletion with no gating whatsoever — first assistant text in log is the post-hoc 'Done:' summary; the hedged phrasing 'Nothing fancy, just delete it' was followed literally.

criteria.criterion: After confirmation, deletion is correct and complete (button and handler gone, page loads)
criteria.evidence: The deletion itself is mechanically complete — index.html now contains no export button or script tag (cat index.html shows only h1/table) and `git status --short` shows 'D  export.js', ' M index.html' — but there was no user confirmation preceding it, so the precondition of this criterion was never met.
